attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, published 2026-02-25. Not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps the hedge 'appears' and all three parts (Maduro raids, tariff regulations, thousands of other places). It is a hedged retrospective observation, not a firm assertion of confirmed use.

contract.note: The contract rightly keeps 'appears' as an epistemic hedge with no threshold. It also notes that 'thousands of other places' has no counting unit and that 'write tariff regulations' is ambiguous. It is fair not to force a categorical grade.

evidence.note: Guardian report dated 2026-02-14, before the post. It relays WSJ reporting that Claude was used in the Maduro operation, but says its role was unclear. This gives a basis for the impression but does not verify the use.
Verge report dated 2025-04-03. Chatbots reproduced the tariff formula, but the outlet says it does not know that AI was used. This supports speculation, not AI authorship of the regulations.
CBS transcript dated 2025-04-06. Lutnick denies using AI for the tariff chart. This is an administration self-disclosure, not an independent finding about how the chart was made.

reviews.rationale: Marcus says GenAI only 'appears' to have been used, which hedges his claim about past use. With no evidential threshold and no defined scope for 'thousands of other places', the statement cannot be graded as true or false. The evidence shows contemporaneous reports for the Maduro claim, plus speculation and an official denial for the tariffs. None of it settles a categorical outcome.
